profile.headline: Software Engineer @ SpaceX | Berkeley EECS Alum
profile.summary:
Software Engineer graduated from UC Berkeley with a strong passion in programming and engineering, especially in system programming, operating system, distributed systems, networking & security. As an ambitious and motivated individual, I yearn for opportunities to broaden my horizons, make self-improvements through multiple challenges as well as contribute to the future of technology and the humanity.

In my free time, I enjoy building projects, solving coding problems, and learning new technologies that I'm interested in!

Feel free to contact me at ducnguyen10214@berkeley.edu to discuss just about anything software related!

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Pioneered the per-beam KPI reporting infrastructure for the Direct To Cell constellation that processes 100M+ KPI records daily from 650+ LEO satellites. This system is the core data source for diagnosing global DTC network performance and driving key optimizations, e.g., beam restart time, handover efficiency, UE admission procedures, etc.
- Architected the non-terrestrial Public Warning System (PWS) that overcomes original challenges, including complex geographic accuracy mapping, high-latency links, and beam-switch integrity, to ensure regulatory compliance across US, Japan, Canada, and Australia. Partnered cross-functionally with MME and external operator-specific engineering teams to define and validate optimal system behaviors.
- Spearheaded the end-to-end Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) functionalities for Direct To Cell satellite beams, achieving 98% beam availability with 99% beam reliability across 650+ LEO satellites serving 5 continents. Engineered a filtering system for custom and dynamic stack configurations to facilitate operator demands. Developed a heartbeat monitor to enforce regulatory compliance and prevent unauthorized cross-border transmissions.
- Redesigned the Inter-Frequency Handover (IFHO) and Radio Resource Control (RRC) procedures to optimize system and UE behavior in a high-velocity LEO environment. Implemented dynamic measConfig–event mapping, release with redirect, and RSRP hysteresis tuning, achieving 80% inter-frequency HO success rate with 90% beam-ping reliability while significantly reducing the ping-pong effect.

positions.title: CS162 Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
- Conducted discussion sections and design reviews for students to improve their understanding of course materials and system design skills in the course about Operating Systems and Systems Programming at UC Berkeley.
- Graded exams, projects, and hold office hours while actively debugging and providing invaluable feedback to the esteemed course staff, contributing to the continuous improvement and excellence of the course.

company.name: UC Berkeley Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences (EECS)

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern - Data Infrastructure
positions.locationName: Long Beach, California, United States · On-site
positions.description:
- Orchestrated a Resource Description Framework to manage over 20GB of metadata per month by leveraging Terraform, CI/CD, Kubernetes, and the graph database Amazon Neptune with Amazon S3.
- Spearheaded the entire development lifecycle of the data pipeline, including migrating data from InfluxDB and MongoDB to Neptune by using Apache Kafka and Amazon Lambda.
- Achieved an exceptional 10-fold query performance optimization through a combination of optimization tech- niques, auto-scaling based on changing workload demands, and Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.

positions.title: Systems Research Engineer
positions.description:
- Collaborated with Dr. Dor Bitan in designing a cross-platform application that relies on the zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) algorithm tailored for legal and privacy use cases. The main goal is to verify the truthfulness or existence of information without revealing its content.
- Leveraged Cassandra to function as a scalable and distributed storage of ZKP-related data, ensuring data durability and supporting auditing and tracking requirements when necessary.
- Incorporated Redis as the core caching layer to provide quick access to segments of shared materials and ZKP metadata, enhancing the efficiency of the algorithm by 5 times and significantly reducing its computation time for each iteration.

company.name: Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing

positions.title: EECS16A Lab Tutor
positions.description: - Demonstrated exceptional support to 50 students in lab assignments and conceptual inquiries throughout 11 weekly labs in the well-known EECS 16A: Designing Information Devices and Systems I course at UC Berkeley.
